evidence: Wikipedia's article on 'Word Crimes' (2014, on 'Mandatory Fun'): it parodies Robin Thicke's 'Blurred Lines' featuring Pharrell Williams and T.I., and peaked at number 39 on the Billboard Hot 100. Yankovic said many fan parodies of the song had been about its rape controversy and he chose grammar instead, a subject no one had used.

earlier.artist: Robin Thicke featuring T.I. and Pharrell
earlier.title: Blurred Lines

trackPair.whatToListenFor: 'Blurred Lines' is a bouncy, whistling, cowbell groove. 'Word Crimes' keeps it and fills it with rules about grammar and spelling. Listen to how a party groove carries a lecture.

explanation.age13: 'Word Crimes' copies 'Blurred Lines' and turns it into a song about grammar mistakes. Weird Al chose grammar on purpose, because the original song had been criticised for how it talked about women.
explanation.adult: Yankovic sidestepped the original's controversy rather than satirising it, by his own account. The source song lost a copyright case to Marvin Gaye's estate the year after.
